title: Composition coherence of the specified coefficient pullback comparisons
statement: Fix a prime ℓ, a field k of prime characteristic different from ℓ, a finite coefficient field E inside PadicAlgCl ℓ, and separated schemes X,Y,X′,Y′ of finite type over k. Let f:X→Y, g:Y′→Y, f′:X′→Y′ and g′:X′→X be k-morphisms with g′≫f=f′≫g. Use the bounded constructible categories, pullbacks and square comparison θ_A of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and scalar extension T and the specified pullback comparisons α_h of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-comparisons]. For each V in C_E(Y), α_f′(Lg_E V)⁻¹, followed by T_X′(θ_E(V)) and α_g′(Lf_E V), equals Lf′_Ω(α_g(V)), followed by θ_Ω(T_Y V) and Lg′_Ω(α_f(V)⁻¹). Here both paths start at Lf′_Ω(T_Y′(Lg_E V)) and end at Lg′_Ω(T_X(Lf_E V)). No properness, Cartesianity, push comparison or exchange morphism is assumed.

proof.text: Specialize the proved generic derived_pull_comp calculation in ContinuousIntegralPullComposition to the flat condensed coefficient map E → PadicAlgCl ℓ. That calculation derives restriction/pushforward composition and conjugates through the scalar and geometric adjunctions, so it applies to this coefficient map independently of the integral specialization in that module. Apply Iso.ext and ObjectProperty.hom_ext. The private projection equations identify restricted scalar-extension and pullback maps and objects with their ambient derived counterparts. Use the proved bounded_comp_hom calculation to identify the bounded composition constraints. Evaluate the generic natural-transformation equality at K.obj, normalize the restricted functor projections, and use congruence to obtain qbarPullIso_comp.

The pull comparison respects equality of geometric morphisms: substitute the equality, after which both transports are reflexive isomorphisms and the functorial unit identities close the equation. This is qbarPull_eq.

Apply qbarPullIso_comp to g′ followed by f and to f′ followed by g. Use qbarPull_eq for sq.w.symm. Expand only the component API of boundedConstructiblePullbackSquareComparison into inverse composition, equality transport, and forward composition. Paste the three isomorphism equalities with the elementary mapped_iso_rectangle calculation already proved in ContinuousIntegralExchangeTargetAdjunct. This yields qbarPull_square_cube_iso.

Take hom components of the isomorphism equality. Cancel the isomorphism α_f′ on the left and the image of α_f on the right using the elementary inverse_mapped_square calculation, obtaining exactly the stated inverse-α_f′ orientation. This uses no exchange morphism, push comparison, properness, or Cartesianity.

theorem constructibleToQbar_pullback_cube
    (sq : CommSq g' f' f g) (V : PadicSubfieldConstructible Y ℓ E) :
    (constructibleToQbarPullIso ℓ k E f'
      ((boundedConstructibleUpperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) ℓ k g).obj V)).inv ≫
      (constructibleToPadicAlgCl X' ℓ E).map
        ((boundedConstructiblePullbackSquareComparison
          (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) ℓ k sq).hom.app V) ≫
      (constructibleToQbarPullIso ℓ k E g'
        ((boundedConstructibleUpperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) ℓ k f).obj V)).hom =
    (boundedConstructibleUpperStar (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) ℓ k f').map
      (constructibleToQbarPullIso ℓ k E g V).hom ≫
      (boundedConstructiblePullbackSquareComparison (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ)
        ℓ k sq).hom.app ((constructibleToPadicAlgCl Y ℓ E).obj V) ≫
      (boundedConstructibleUpperStar (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) ℓ k g').map
        (constructibleToQbarPullIso ℓ k E f V).inv
